persona: Calm nurse who works late shifts and drives home through the country roads north-west of Auckland. Starts the report without signing in and signs in when asked to upload. Has not noticed that the body shop typed the registration wrong.
initial_message: Hi, I hit a wild pig on a country road near Kaukapakapa on Monday 7 September at about 9:40pm, driving home from work. The front bumper is cracked, the grille is broken and one fog light is smashed. I wasn't hurt and the car is still drivable. The pig ran off into the bush.

facts.incident.description: I was driving home from a late shift on a rural road. A wild pig ran out of the scrub onto the road right in front of me. I braked but hit it with the front left of the car. It ran off into the bush and I drove home carefully.
facts.incident.cause: A wild pig ran onto the road in front of the car
facts.loss.description: Front bumper cracked, lower grille broken and left fog light smashed
facts.policyholder.name: Ravi Tidewell
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Front bumper cracked and pushed in on the left side, lower grille broken, left fog light smashed, with mud and coarse hair caught in the cracks
facts.driver.name: Ravi Tidewell
facts.if_asked_about_the_animal: It was a wild pig, not anyone's stock. There were no farm buildings or fences nearby, just bush. It ran away.
facts.if_asked_about_the_registration_on_the_q: Oh, I didn't notice that. My car is TST-047; they must have mixed up the numbers.
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the front of the car taken in my garage the next morning. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Harbourside Panel & Paint dated 9 September 2026, total $2,323.00 including GST. Available now.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in a home garage in morning light, close-up of the lower front left corner of a black hatchback, seen from the front left. The plastic front bumper is cracked and pushed in, the black honeycomb lower grille beside it is broken, and the round fog light in the bumper corner is smashed, with dried mud and coarse dark bristly hair caught in the cracks. The frame shows only the bumper corner, the fog light, part of the lower grille and the front tyre; the centre of the bumper is outside the frame. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.

design.notes: The repair quote prints the registration TST-074; the claimant's car and the policy schedule are TST-047 (digits transposed). The mismatch is unrelated to dates, so no review indicator applies. The claimant starts without signing in and signs in before the first upload.

triage.rationale: The repair quote names registration TST-074, while the claimant and the policy schedule give TST-047. The material contradicts the statement and nothing in the pack corrects the quote, so someone must follow it up. It is not a date conflict, so the review indicators stay none. A wild animal is not another party; nobody hurt, car drivable, one clear photo, quote NZD 2,323.00 including GST. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

prior_claims_12m.basis: Starts anonymous, signs in before upload; the account has no earlier claims

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 July 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2023-07-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
